question.text: For a reversible reaction <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>⇌</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>, the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>∆</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math> forward reaction <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kJ</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The activation energy of the uncatalyzed forward reaction is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>300</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kJ</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. When the reaction is catalysed keeping the reactant concentration same, the rate of the catalysed forward reaction at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>27</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is found to be same as that of the uncatalyzed reaction at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>327</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. The activation energy of the catalysed backward reaction is _______<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo> </mo><mi>kJ</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

solution.text:
As per the question 

To determine the activation energy of the catalyzed backward reaction, we need to use the Arrhenius equation and the given information.

The Arrhenius equation is given by: 

k=Ae(-Ea/RT)

Ae-300×103600×R=Ae-Ea300×R

⇒1032=Ea300

⇒Ea=150×103J mol–1

⇒Ea=150 kJ mol–1

∴ Activation energy of catalysed backward reaction

Energy of activation for backward reactionEb=Ea-∆H

=150-20=130 kJ mol–1
